notes.claim: When an exponential equation cannot be rewritten with a common base, it is solved by taking the logarithm of each side.
Once the exponential term is isolated, take the logarithm of both sides, then use the power rule to bring the unknown down as a factor.

sources.title: 6.6 Exponential and Logarithmic Equations - College Algebra | OpenStax
sources.quote: Sometimes the terms of an exponential equation cannot be rewritten with a common base. In these cases, we solve by taking the logarithm of each side.

sources.quote: Since the exponential is isolated, take the logarithm of both sides.
